title: Rolling cycle headroom matrix & contingency orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle shocks (unplanned enterprise deals, outages, or increased infra costs) repeatedly force either risky all-hands triage or ad-hoc scope cuts. We lack a compact, actionable artifact that an initiative owner and the on-call capacity manager can use to decide where to trim, how much buffer to preserve, and which features can be deferred with the least OKR impact.

Goal: Deliver a pragmatic "headroom matrix" artifact plus a matching contingency orchestration runbook that: (1) codifies per-initiative headroom targets based on historical delivery variance and OKR criticality, (2) provides a deterministic priority-bucket mapping for potential scope cuts, (3) defines a lightweight decision flow for triggering staff reallocation or scope deferral, and (4) supplies templates for communications and post-mortem analysis.

Scope: Product initiatives (all PM-owned initiatives across cycles), cross-functional staffing (engineers, design, SRE on rotation), and the CycleOps process. Implementation includes the headroom matrix spreadsheet, a one-page playbook, a short simulation harness to validate tradeoffs for three representative weeks, and a rollout plan for Q2 cycle planning workshops.

Out of scope: Deep tooling integration into the Console or automated staffing swaps (these are follow-ups).

Deliverables:
- Headroom matrix (Google Sheets) with per-initiative recommended headroom percentage, recommended contingency actions, and expected OKR delta.
- Contingency orchestration playbook (1–2 pages) with decision gates, stakeholders, and communication templates.
- Simulation report (3 scenario runs) showing tradeoffs between latency of delivery and OKR attainment.
- Workshop materials and one training session for PM owners and EMs.

Success metrics:
- 80% of initiatives have a documented headroom value and contingency mapping before cycle kickoff.
- In two subsequent mid-cycle shocks, decision time to final scope cut reduced from median 2 days to <8 hours.
- Less than 10% increase in severity of OKR regressions versus prior cycles when contingency applied.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sheet populated for top 20 initiatives with clear rationale, owner, and fallback action.
- Playbook reviewed by at least 3 PM leads and 2 Eng EMs and updated based on feedback.
- Simulation artifacts checked in to the CycleOps drive and linked in the ticket.

Risks: Subjectivity in prioritization; cross-team coordination overhead; potential for overly conservative headroom causing systematic over-reserving of capacity. Mitigations: explicit scoring rubric, quarterly calibration session, and monitoring of reserved capacity utilization for adjustments.
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with PM leads and EMs. Agreed scope and success metrics. Action: PMs to nominate top 20 initiatives by 2026-02-18. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/CycleOps/headroom-kickoff

2026-02-15: Received initial initiative list from Product. Noted heavy concentration in Platform and Dedicated. Action: run variance analysis on 12 months of delivery velocity (ENG to provide data pull). Assigned to Liam Chen.
2026-02-18: ENG provided velocity export and incident history. Preliminary variance model shows median slippage of 18% across initiatives; used as baseline for headroom suggestions.
2026-02-20: Draft headroom matrix created (v0.1). Shared with PM review group. Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/placeholder-headroom

2026-02-23: PM feedback: prefer explicit mapping of OKR-critical vs. nice-to-have flags; suggested three contingency tiers (soft defer, scoped trim, full defer). Action: incorporate tiers and run first simulation.

2026-02-26: Simulation run 1 (short-term outage scenario) completed. Results show recommended average headroom 22% for high-variance initiatives. Uploaded report: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/CycleOps/headroom-sim1.pdf

2026-02-28: Playbook draft circulated for review. Next steps: finalize sheet v1.0, run two additional sims, schedule 60m workshop during cycle planning week. Owner: Aisha Kapoor. Updated_at set to 2026-02-28.
decision_log: Decision 2026-02-11: Use historical delivery variance + OKR criticality to compute suggested headroom instead of pure absolute staff buffer.

Decision 2026-02-23: Adopt three contingency tiers with deterministic cut rules: Tier A (soft defer features with <5% OKR impact), Tier B (trim scopes reducing >5% but <20% OKR delta), Tier C (full defer non-critical initiatives).
Open decision 2026-02-26: Whether to expose headroom recommendations in the CycleOps dashboard (deferred to follow-up).
Follow-up 2026-02-28: Schedule calibration session for 2026-Q2 retro to review utilization and adjust heuristics.
notes: Template: include a short rationale field per initiative and a conservative/optimistic headroom column to help PMs choose policy.
Plan to run a light-weight pilot with 6 initiatives in March prior to broad rollout.
If pilot shows consistent underutilization of reserved headroom (>60% unused two cycles in a row), reduce target headroom by 25% for next cycle.
